subject: 2024-2025 Council Governing Agenda Review
overview: The City Council Committee of the Whole met to conduct a mid-year review of the 2024-2025 Council Governing Agenda across its various standing committees. No formal legislative action was taken, and the paper was kept in committee.

items.title: Review of 2024-2025 Council Governing Agenda
items.summary: The Council opened discussion on Paper 24-006 to evaluate progress made on its governing agenda goals and prepare an updated document for public distribution in January.

items.title: Administration and Finance Committee Review
items.summary: President Bears reported on key financial milestones, including the implementation of the new budget ordinance, passage of Proposition 2.5 overrides, establishment of stabilization funds, and pending linkage fee legislation.

items.title: Education and Culture and Governance Committees Review
items.summary: The Council reviewed work on student internship opportunities and discussed the upcoming review process for the draft charter revision submitted by the mayor.

items.title: Planning and Permitting Committee Review
items.summary: Vice President Collins provided an update on comprehensive zoning updates across city neighborhoods, including the ordained Mystic Avenue Corridor, the ongoing Salem Street Corridor review, and proposed green score standards.

items.title: Public Health and Community Safety Committee Review
items.summary: Councilor Lazzaro highlighted passed measures on wildlife feeding, plant medicine decriminalization, and surveillance ordinance amendments, alongside planned work on rodent control and health care protections.

items.title: Public Works and Facilities Committee Review
items.summary: Councilor Callahan outlined scheduled DPW reports on road and sidewalk infrastructure, lead pipe replacement efforts, public restroom access, and a proposed volunteer tree planting program.

items.title: Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee Review
items.summary: Councilor Leming detailed progress on City Council communication upgrades, community listening sessions, the welcoming ordinance, and veteran rental assistance, after which the main paper was retained in committee.
